phase_0.boundary_condition: the modulus N and the ring Z/NZ over the SIXTEEN_3 substrate close the protocol, with the reconstructed N as the terminal anchor
phase_0.domain_name: semiprime factor extraction protocol on SIXTEEN_3 source N split
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.justification: the unit 1 moves forward into the idempotent arm e that carries one factor of N

AREV.justification: the unit 1 descends into the complementary arm 1-e that carries the other factor of N

CLINK.justification: the extracted factors are chained into the product that reconstructs N

ENGAGR.justification: the zero product and the sum e+(1-e)=1 are held together as simultaneous constraints

EVALF.justification: the negative arm touches (1-e)^2=1-e and the projection of the other factor

EVALT.justification: the affirmative arm touches e^2=e and the projection of one factor

FFUSE.justification: the e and 1-e arms rejoin into one closed modulus N

FSPLIT.justification: the unit opens into the two idempotent arms e and 1-e

IFIX.justification: the extracted factors are appended permanently to the protocol record

IMSCRIB.justification: N is self-recognized as the same modulus before and after the split and fuse

TANCH.justification: the ring Z/NZ contains all residue operations and the final reconstructed N seals the boundary

VINIT.justification: N is present before any idempotent arm is named, so the factor extraction state is void of projections

phase_2.fuse_result: single closed modulus N with extracted factors p and q attached
phase_2.rejoin_note: the e arm extracts p by gcd(e,N), the 1-e arm extracts q by gcd(1-e,N), orthogonality is evaluated, and the arms rejoin by CRT into N
phase_2.split_input: source semiprime N with its unit 1
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11): the live register where e and 1-e are held together
phase_3.false_description: B4 F (10): the negative register for the 1-e arm
phase_3.true_description: B4 T (01): the affirmative register for the e arm
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00): neither, the empty register before any idempotent arm is named

steps.domain_action: source semiprime N enters the SIXTEEN_3 substrate as an unprocessed modulus
N is recognized as itself in the ring Z/NZ
unit 1 opens into idempotent arms e and 1-e
e arm is evaluated for idempotence e^2=e
orthogonality e(1-e)=0 and completeness e+(1-e)=1 are held together
e arm advances to factor p by gcd(e,N)
1-e arm descends to factor q by gcd(1-e,N)
p and q are composed into the product p*q
the two factor arms rejoin into the single modulus N
the extracted factor pair p and q is appended to the immutable record
the protocol closes at the sealed boundary of N

phase_5.alfs_store: the canonical reference is the ring Z/NZ with unit 1 and the CRT isomorphism
phase_5.compiler_frontend: the protocol compiler translates a semiprime N and a candidate idempotent e into modular ring operations
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: the e and 1-e arms communicate through shared residue classes modulo N
phase_5.memory_mechanism: state is stored as N, e, 1-e, p, q, and the orthogonality relation
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the scheduler orders initialization, split, arm evaluation, orthogonality, fusion, and fixation

phase_6.cycle_cost: one modular setup, two idempotence evaluations, two gcd extractions, and one CRT reconstruction per cycle
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0: the split and fuse preserve the information content of N while moving it between arms
phase_6.post_cycle_state: N is closed with e, 1-e, p, q, and the orthogonality relation recorded
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: N is loaded as a semiprime modulus with unit 1 and no idempotent arm named
